cards.title: Constraints as Creative Fuel
cards.insight: Severe limitations—time, budget, or resources—paradoxically unlock creative breakthroughs by forcing prioritization and novel problem-solving. When scope is narrow, imagination must expand to fill the gap, often yielding simpler, more elegant solutions than unconstrained projects.
cards.takeaway: When facing resource limits, reframe them as creative challenges rather than obstacles; define your smallest viable experiment first.

cards.title: Collision as Catalyst
cards.insight: Breakthrough ideas often emerge at the intersection of unrelated fields or perspectives. The friction between different disciplines, cultures, or viewpoints creates cognitive tension that pushes thinkers beyond established patterns and assumptions.
cards.takeaway: Deliberately seek input from people outside your domain; schedule cross-functional conversations to challenge your default thinking.

cards.title: Failure as Data, Not Verdict
cards.insight: Creative work thrives in environments where unsuccessful attempts are treated as information rather than judgment. Rapid iteration with low stakes builds confidence, reveals hidden insights, and normalizes experimentation as part of the process.
cards.takeaway: Track what didn't work and why; share failed prototypes with collaborators to accelerate collective learning.

cards.title: Boredom as a Fallow Field
cards.insight: Sustained creative output requires periods of apparent inactivity—mind-wandering, reflection, and rest—not just execution. The subconscious continues processing and connecting ideas when conscious effort pauses, often surfacing unexpected connections.
cards.takeaway: Build buffer time into projects; protect space for unstructured thinking as essential to creative depth, not a luxury.
